title: Money, and who is in charge of it

cues.text: Part Two starts from nothing again. Nothing here assumes you know what a central bank is, or an interest rate, or a bond. We build all of them from scratch, exactly as we built cost and revenue.

And there is one new person. This is Kit. He is a student, and the argument in this half of the film is his. He notices things, gets excited about them, and then talks himself down when the evidence will not carry him. That last part is the whole point of Part Two.
central bank. The public body that looks after a country's money. The Bank of England is ours.
interest. The extra a borrower pays a lender for the use of the money.
Here is what an interest rate means, with numbers. Borrow a hundred pounds at five per cent, and you pay back a hundred and five after a year.
interest rate. How much extra, as a percentage per year.
monetary policy. The things a central bank does to make borrowing easier or harder across the whole country.
Meet the Governor. He runs the central bank. He is well-meaning, he holds the levers, and he is genuinely trying to help. He is not the villain of this film. There isn't one.
After the crash of two thousand and eight, the Bank wanted people and businesses to spend and build. So it did the usual thing. It cut the rate.
And it cut it again. And again.
And by two thousand and nine the rate was almost at zero. The lever had hit the floor. You cannot cut much below nothing.
So they needed something else. That something else is the subject of the next chapter.
